author: Evagrius Ponticus
occasion: A spiritual father offers practical and ascetical guidance to a virgin living in a Christian community, urging her to guard her purity, humility, and devotion to Christ as her heavenly bridegroom.
argument: The work is a series of short counsels urging a consecrated virgin to love and serve Christ, honor her mother and sisters, and avoid the dangers that threaten her calling: encounters with men, anger, luxury, gossip, and worldly distractions. She is to practice constant prayer, tears, humility, and self-control, while trusting in Christ as her true bridegroom. Evagrius warns that vices such as envy, slander, greed, and lack of mercy will extinguish her lamp and keep her from seeing her bridegroom, whereas purity, meekness, and faithful endurance will win her an eternal crown. The final sections contrast the fate of faithful virgins with that of the impure, and close with a call to remember Christ and the Holy Trinity.

outline.move: Opening counsels on love for Christ, honoring mother and sisters, reading at sunrise and work after the second hour, constant prayer, avoiding encounters with men, and basic discipline of food, speech, and humility.
Further warnings against vainglory, anger, disobedience, worldly dress and company, and encouragement to secret tears in the night, faith, and humility.

Counsels on guarding the heart from evil thoughts, psalmody, the foolish virgin's love of silver versus the wise virgin's generosity, and the dangers of sorrow, listlessness, slander, and drawing out words with laughter from a man.
Final exhortations on humility, endurance in self-control, fidelity to church teaching, and the promised reward of the virgin soul united with Christ the bridegroom.

cast.name: Evagrius
cast.who: The author and spiritual father addressing the virgin as his child.

cast.name: The Virgin
cast.who: The consecrated virgin to whom the exhortation is addressed.

cast.name: Christ
cast.who: The Lord and heavenly bridegroom of the virgin soul.

voices.speaker: Evagrius
voices.how_marked: First-person address occurs only in the closing section (u01-rem-close); the rest of the work uses second-person imperative address without first-person markers

key_terms.sense: A consecrated virgin, dedicated to Christ
Christ as the heavenly bridegroom of the virgin soul
The lamp of the virgin soul, kept burning with the oil of good works and mercy
Oil for the lamp, symbolizing mercy and good works
The bridal chamber, the place of union with Christ
Listlessness or spiritual torpor that oppresses the soul
Self-control, especially in food and bodily discipline
Moderation and chastity of soul and body
Freedom from disordered passions, a state of spiritual calm
The mind or understanding, purified by vigil and prayer
Thoughts, especially evil or tempting thoughts that defile the heart
Prayer, especially pure and constant prayer
The Holy Trinity, to be remembered and worshipped

scripture: The work contains no explicit biblical citations, but its imagery of lamps, oil, the bridegroom, and the bridal chamber draws on the Gospel parable of the ten virgins (Matthew 25:1-13). Psalm numbering follows the Septuagint where applicable.
uncertain: The precise date of composition is uncertain, though Evagrius's literary activity is generally placed in the late fourth century.
The identity of the addressee beyond her being a consecrated virgin is unknown.
